market_summary: US markets are processing a major patent verdict against Apple, while Alphabet/Google faces regulatory challenges in Europe. <cite index="1-1">A San Diego jury handed Taction Technology a $5,721,961,750 verdict against Apple on September 25, 2026, over two patents covering the haptic technology used in the iPhone and Apple Watch's Taptic Engine.

items.headline: Apple hit with record $5.7 billion verdict in Taction haptic patent case; plans appeal
items.summary: <cite index="1-1">A San Diego jury handed Taction Technology a $5,721,961,750 verdict against Apple over two patents covering the haptic technology used in the iPhone and Apple Watch's Taptic Engine.</cite> <cite index="1-4">Apple said it would appeal.</cite>

items.headline: Google challenges EU orders requiring it to share search data and open Android to AI rivals
items.summary: <cite index="11-2">Alphabet's Google has challenged two EU orders to help AI rivals such as OpenAI access its services and search engine competitors to access its search data, saying these would undermine privacy safeguards and cause irreversible harm to European users.</cite> <cite index="12-6">Google filed two challenges with the EU's General Court on September 28.</cite>

items.headline: Daivio launches AI-powered data analysis workload for Microsoft Fabric
items.summary: <cite index="42-1">Daivio, the AI analyst for Microsoft Fabric, is available now in the Microsoft Fabric Workload Hub and on Microsoft Marketplace.</cite> The tool enables analysts to clean data and get answers in plain language without leaving Fabric.

items.headline: Microsoft Fabric available for GCC High customers; general AI data analytics platform expanding
items.summary: <cite index="37-3,37-4">Microsoft Fabric will be available in public preview for GCC High customers, with general availability starting October 1, 2026.</cite> The platform continues to roll out AI-powered data analytics features.

items.headline: Nvidia launches Open Agent Safety Platform for AI security; partners with Arm and Intel
items.summary: <cite index="28-1,28-2">NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform consists of NVIDIA OpenShell open source software and the NVIDIA Sentry reference system design that enables full-stack governance and control across software and hardware, compute and robotics systems that run agents.</cite> <cite index="30-1">Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform demonstrates this approach, with Arm-compatible compute running agent workloads and independent Arm-based DPUs helping observe, isolate and protect them.</cite>

items.headline: Fed rate hike benefits Singapore banks; DBS, OCBC, UOB among biggest winners
items.summary: <cite index="23-3,23-4,23-5">On 16 September 2026, the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points to a 3.75%–4.00% target range — its first hike since 2023. While Wall Street retreated, Singapore's Straits Times Index rose 0.5%. The reason: DBS, OCBC, and UOB — which together make up roughly 40–54% of the STI — are among the biggest beneficiaries of rising rates.</cite>

items.headline: Singapore shares end higher as bank counters rise; STI up 0.3%
items.summary: Singapore's Straits Times Index rose 0.3% with banking stocks leading gains, reflecting positive sentiment following Fed rate developments and continued wealth management momentum in the sector.

items.headline: HK-listed engineering firm Metasurface files for dual primary listing on Catalist
items.summary: Hong Kong-listed Metasurface has filed for a dual primary listing on the SGX Catalist, signaling continued international interest in Singapore's growth and innovation-focused exchange platform.

items.headline: Keppel and StarHub in discussions on potential M1 deal
items.summary: Keppel and StarHub are in discussions regarding a potential merger deal involving M1, representing significant telecom consolidation activity in Singapore's market.
